evidence: De La Soul's 'Freedom of Speak (We Got Three Minutes)', the B-side of their 'Plug Tunin'' single (1988), samples Syl Johnson's 1967 'Different Strokes' alongside several James Brown records, as catalogued by sample-credit databases including WhoSampled.

later.title: Freedom of Speak (We Got Three Minutes)

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Johnson's original is a tight, live soul-funk groove built around a drum break and a spoken 'different strokes for different folks' hook. De La Soul chops it into just a fragment inside a dense collage, one voice among several sources rather than the whole beat, the same reuse-as-texture approach 'Different Strokes' would get from dozens of other producers.

explanation: Syl Johnson's 1967 song 'Different Strokes' has been sampled by more hip-hop producers than almost any other record. De La Soul used a piece of it on 'Freedom of Speak', from the same 1988 single as 'Plug Tunin'', the demo that got them signed. It is one credited use among dozens: acts across this map, Wu-Tang Clan and Public Enemy among them, have sampled it, which is part of why Johnson later called himself, without much exaggeration, the most sampled man in music history.
